summary:
Turn 30 produced a clean C1 artifact whose checker set contains only the in-scope properties, which is the second route identified last turn for closing the open scope issue.

Why this shape. The open issue ef6b54abce294555b31a3c9a6ca606ac is a bookkeeping problem on the fixed artifact 05dc6a36…, which asserts an applied-state predicate that the accepted C1 scope excludes. The proposition itself is already carried and confirmed as claim C3-applied-effect-follows-committed-vector (artifact 52a176de…, reviewed with no issue). The two rejected mechanisms were an ordinary repair (which must preserve oracle, prerequisites and legality) and an encoding correction (which needs an oracle or observation challenge rather than a scope challenge); F2 was judged unnecessary because the C1 scope already excludes execution. What remained was a fresh artifact on the same unit whose plan selects only the three in-scope properties.

What was submitted. action=check on unit-C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector with plan-recovery-divergence.json, whose monitors and observable properties are exactly the reviewed three: adoption at the resolution (adopted_committed), the recoverer-versus-committed-peer comparison (vectors_match), and agreement across the three replicas after the Commit broadcast (all_committed_match), each with the committed_reply prerequisite as admission alias, instance identity correlation and the same grounding. The harness bytes are the driven version that re-reads InstanceSpace after every delivery; it still prints the applied-state event, but no monitor selects it, so the executed checker set no longer asserts anything outside the accepted scope. The requirement, applicability, prerequisites, oracle wording and harness rounds are otherwise unchanged, so the artifact is a clean re-execution of the confirmed finding rather than a weakening of it.

Next step. Once the trusted runner executes this artifact and a correspondence review accepts it, it becomes the natural target for resolving the open issue: it is the C1 artifact that contains only in-scope predicates, so the resolution can state that the disputed property belongs to C3 while C1's own artifact set is clean. Audit spec version 6 stands, both other claims are untouched, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
